description: Dutch (Netherlands) terminology, register, and audit allowlist for the AlgaPSA nl locale.

domainTerms.notes: Keep account as the established Dutch software term (het account, de accounts) for user, MSP, and customer accounts.
Use afspraak for calendar appointments and afspraakverzoek for appointment requests; use inplannen when emphasizing the scheduling action.
Use goedkeuring for approval workflows, requests, invoices, and timesheets; use goedkeuren for the action.

Keep asset (de asset, de assets) for managed devices, inventory, and configuration assets. Activa and bezit occur in the current files but have financial/property senses and are inconsistent with the dominant MSP term. Reserve activa strictly for accounting/financial prose, never as the managed-asset entity label.
Use toewijzing for assigning tickets, tasks, users, or technicians; use toewijzen for the action.
Use for workflow automation and automated operational behavior.
Use facturatie for the billing product area and billing settings. Facturering is also frequent and should be reserved for the invoicing process where a distinction is useful.
Use bord/borden for ticket and kanban boards. Board remains in a few current strings; never use bestuur, which means a governing board.

Use urenbundel for prepaid or retainer hour pools and verbruiksbundel for consumption pools. Current contracts, catalog, billing, and reports establish bundel; literal emmer and untranslated bucket remnants are inconsistent.
Use begroting for project or financial budgets and spending limits. A sales quote is an offerte.
Use klant/klanten for customer organizations and client-portal users. Cliënt appears in current files but is not the dominant PSA/IT term.
Use the closed compound klantenportaal for the customer-facing app. Klantportaal occurs once but klantenportaal dominates.
Use opmerking for ticket, project, task, and document comments. Reactie is appropriate only when the source specifically means a reply/reaction.
Use contact for the CRM record and compact field labels; use contactpersoon when the person must be explicit. Do not translate the noun as contact opnemen met, which is a verb phrase.
Use contract for service contracts, contract templates, and contract lines.

Use contractregel for billable contract lines — dominant in the app (~205 contractregel vs ~13 contractlijn) and more idiomatic. Normalize remaining contractlijn occurrences. Adversarial review 2026-08.
Use krediet for customer credits, available credit, and credit application; use saldo or restant when referring only to the remaining balance.
Keep dashboard as the established Dutch software loanword (het dashboard).
Area label is Planning; the dispatch board is the planbord (Dynamics Field Service convention). Use technicusplanning only when the technician scope must be explicit.
Use document for uploaded documents, folders, sharing, and document management.
Spell the noun e-mail with a hyphen; use E-mail at the start of a label or sentence and e-mails in the plural.
Use the closed compound e-mailadres for one address and e-mailadressen for the plural.
Use e-mailtype for the label/type picker on an email row, matching the contacts namespace.
Use extensie for platform/product extensions and installed extension metadata.
Use bestand for uploaded and generated files; use map for folders.
Use filter as the UI noun and filteren for the action.
Use afhandeling for the sales-order fulfillment column and the matching customer-document label; levering is the physical delivery and is a different concept.
Use branche for the client/CRM business vertical (Dynamics NL convention). industrie reads as manufacturing; sector is acceptable in broader prose. Adversarial review 2026-08.
Use factuur for customer invoices and conceptfactuur for a draft invoice.
Use facturering for the invoice-generation process. The current navigation also uses facturatie for this area; keep facturatie as the broader billing label.
Use achtergrondtaak for the background-job entity and taak where context is already clear. msp/jobs currently mixes taak, job, baan, and vacature; baan/vacature are false friends for employment.
Use kennisbank for KB articles, categories, and review flows.
Use licentie for software licensing, seats, and activation.
Use locatie for client, inventory, and service locations.
Use mijlpaal for project milestones and milestone billing schedules.
Use Mobiel for the compact phone-type label and Mobiel nummer when the field needs an explicit noun.

Use melding/meldingen for generic in-app and email notifications. Client-portal.json and notification settings currently use notificatie, while melding dominates elsewhere; do not mix both within one workflow.
Keep onboarding as the established Dutch MSP loanword and form closed compounds such as onboardingwizard, onboardingstap, and onboardingchecklist.
Use betaling for invoice payments, online payments, and payment status.
Use picklijst for the warehouse pick list and gepickt for a picked line: the warehouse anglicism is the accepted Dutch term. Piklijst is a misspelling.
Gebruik salesfunnel voor de commerciële pipeline in het CRM. Nooit pijpleiding of pijplijn: dat is een fysieke buisleiding.
Use Primair e-mailadres as a label and primair e-mailadres in running text.
Use prioriteit for ticket, task, and workflow priority labels.
Use voortgang for progress labels and indicators; the all-caps micro-label is VOORTGANG.
Use project for project management, phases, tasks, budgets, and project templates.
Use offerte/offertes for sales and service quotes. Never citaat, which means a textual quotation.
Use tarief for a priced rate column on customer documents and keep stukprijs for unit price, so a document that shows both columns keeps them distinguishable.
Use rapport for analytics, operational, billing, and audit reports.
Use aanvraag for service, approval, and appointment requests; use aanvragen for the action.

Use planning for the schedule product area and general planned timetable; use inplannen for the action. Schema appears in dispatch and activity namespaces and should be limited to rule/timetable structures.
Use scherm for UI screens and weergave when the source means a view rather than a screen.

Use service for catalog items, managed services, and support services; it is the dominant current term. Dienst is also frequent, especially in billing and ticket namespaces, and should not be mixed within one workflow.
Use the closed compound servicecatalogus for the billing/service catalog product area. Untranslated Service catalog occurs in search strings and is inconsistent.
Use plural instellingen for settings pages and controls.
Keep single sign-on as the established feature name and SSO as the abbreviation; use sentence-style capitalization except where a brand or source title requires otherwise.
Keep SLA as the standard abbreviation; use SLA-overeenkomst only when the expanded entity must be explicit.
Keep status as the accepted Dutch software noun; the plural is statussen.
Use enquête for satisfaction surveys, templates, and response analytics.
Use label/labels for metadata tags; this is the dominant current term. Tag/tags remain in some asset and core strings and should not be introduced into new generic UI copy.
Use taak for project tasks, workflow tasks, and task inbox items. Use achtergrondtaak when a background job must be distinguished from user work.
Use the neutral belasting for tax labels on customer documents. Btw is correct only where value-added tax is specifically meant; a tenant may charge a different levy and the label would then lie.
Use technicus for field/service technicians and technician assignment. Monteur appears once in dispatch copy and is more mechanical/trade-specific.
Keep tenant in admin, security, and integration contexts. Never huurder, which is the real-estate sense; use klant only when the customer organization is meant.
Keep ticket as the MSP support term (het ticket, de tickets). Never kaartje, which implies a small card or travel/admission ticket.

Use tijdregistratie for the module/process (matches navigation). Use tijdsvermelding for a single time record and "tijd invoeren" for the action (Dynamics NL distinction). tijdinvoer/tijdsinvoer occurrences should converge on these forms.
Use urenstaat for grouped/submitted time entries and approval flows. Urenregistratie appears in one header but urenstaat dominates the workflow.
Use stukprijs for the per-unit price column and tarief for rate; the two must stay distinguishable on documents that show both.
Use gebruiker/gebruikers for application users.
Keep webhook as the technical loanword (de webhook, de webhooks).
Use Werk for the work phone-type label, matching all current contact label sets.
Keep workflow as the established software loanword (de workflow, de workflows). AlgaPSA workflows are n8n-style event automation (triggers, actions, runs), not Jira-style status flows.

forbiddenTerms.reason: Accounting register wrongly used for managed/configuration assets; keep activa for financial prose only.
False friend in the job monitor; baan normally means employment or a track, not a background job.
Plural employment/track sense; background jobs are achtergrondtaken.
False friend for a ticket/kanban board; bestuur means a governing body.
Property/possession sense; managed IT devices and configuration assets use asset.
Untranslated English leak for kanban/ticket boards.
Plural of the untranslated board leak.
Untranslated English leak for prepaid hour pools.
Plural of the untranslated bucket leak.
Wrong sense for a sales quote; citaat is a textual quotation.
Plural wrong-sense sales-quote term; use offertes.
Non-dominant register for this PSA; the customer organization is consistently klant in core workflows.
Plural non-dominant customer term; use klanten.
contractregel is dominant (205:13) and idiomatic for billable contract lines.
Plural of the losing contract-line variant.
Wrong spelling for the established nl-NL UI style; use the hyphenated noun e-mail.
Literal translation of billing bucket; emmer means a physical pail. Use urenbundel or verbruiksbundel.
Real-estate false friend in multitenant software; keep tenant in admin and integration contexts.
Manufacturing register for the CRM business-vertical field; use branche.
Informal address conflicts with the dominant formal u register; current je remnants should not be copied into new strings.
Informal emphatic subject pronoun conflicts with the dominant formal register.
Untranslated English leak for background jobs.
Plural of the untranslated job leak.
Informal object pronoun conflicts with the dominant formal register.
Informal possessive conflicts with the dominant formal register.
Wrong register for a support ticket; kaartje means a small card or travel/admission ticket.
A physical pipe. Use salesfunnel for the CRM sales pipeline, or the loanword pipeline for a technical/processing one (workflow canvas, render pipeline).
A physical pipe. Use salesfunnel for the CRM sales pipeline, or the loanword pipeline for a technical/processing one (workflow canvas, render pipeline).
False friend in the job monitor; vacature means a job opening.

dialectRules.rule: Address users consistently with formal u/uw forms; do not introduce je/jij/jouw forms in new user-facing copy.
dialectRules.notes: Formal u/uw forms dominate the locale overall, especially msp/integrations.json, msp/settings.json, msp/account.json, and features/projects.json. Informal copy remains concentrated in features/tickets.json, client-portal.json, msp/onboarding.json, and common.json and is an existing inconsistency. Formal u/uw is the normalization target, not the current uniform state: portal, tickets and onboarding contain informal pockets (~365 hits) that are cleanup debt.

dialectRules.rule: Use Dutch sentence case for headings and labels; capitalize only the first word, proper names, and abbreviations.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: Primair e-mailadres, Goedkeuring urenstaat, Single sign-on. Do not copy English title case.

dialectRules.rule: Write Dutch compounds as one word and spell e-mail with a hyphen.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: klantenportaal, servicecatalogus, onboardingwizard, ticketprioriteit, e-mailadres, e-mailtype.

dialectRules.rule: Use ticket for support work, klant for the customer, and offerte for a sales quote.
dialectRules.notes: The support entity is het ticket. Kaartje, cliënt, and citaat are audited through forbiddenTerms.

dialectRules.rule: Keep facturatie (billing area), factuur (invoice), facturering (invoicing process), krediet (credit), and urenbundel (bucket) distinct.
dialectRules.notes: These entities coexist in the billing UI; do not collapse them into one generic factuur term or translate bucket literally.

dialectRules.rule: Retain established Dutch MSP/software loanwords when the locale consistently uses them.
dialectRules.notes: Examples: account, asset, dashboard, onboarding, service, status, tenant, ticket, webhook, workflow. Use Dutch plurals where needed: assets, tickets, webhooks, workflows, statussen.

dialectRules.rule: Preserve every {{variable}} exactly as in the English source.
dialectRules.notes: Do not translate placeholders, braces, or variable names.

exact: In Xero: Reports → All Reports → Invoice Details
phase_name, task_description, assigned_to, estimated_hours, due_date, priority, service, task_type, status, tags
identicalAllowlist.notes: This allowlist is intentionally conservative; audit tooling should report English-identical Dutch strings unless they match one of these exact values, case-insensitive established loanwords, or technical patterns.
